comments:
Manuscript found in Nepal and now kept at Otani University Library in Japan ([8S7FDMCJ]: 300, n. 267)

Following fol. 210, there is an extra folio featuring one line in 'bru tsha - an excerpt from Vasubandhu’s Āryadaśabhūmivyākhyāna ('Phags pa sa bcu pa'i rnam par bshad pa) (D3993, 261a6) - followed by five lines in  khyug yig on the recto and one line in khyug yig on the verso. The text in khyug yig is unidentified. It includes a numbered list.

Introduction to the item: [H9MPLMTV]. Item studied as part of [M3J8XFVK].

item_description:
The color images show indigenous catalogue marking in red ink "ka" (volume). Some parts of the texts are marked in yellow, or underlined in red.
Script: 'bru tsha
Lines per folio: 8
Folio numbering with numbers written in letters. From 100, number 100 is written as "+"; from 200, number 200 is written as "≠".
Orthography: 
- Frequent abbreviations (e.g., for mngon sum, thams cad, etc.)
- Frequent superabundant suffix –'a (e.g., dbye', brda', gzhi')
- Frequent absence of g- prefixes (e.g., cig for gcig, sum for gsum)
- Alternative initial prefix (e.g., rngos or sngos for dngos)
- Bindu for m
- Alternative spelling (spyad for dpyad; spyod for dpyod; the tsom for the tshom)
- tsheg always present before shad (or double shad)
